column1: # defaults/brief-lint-rules.tsv - what bin/jg-brief-lint.sh reports in a brief.
# Owner of the row format: this header. Reader: bin/jg-brief-lint.sh (--rules names another table).
# Columns are separated by one TAB; a pattern is a POSIX extended regular expression, `-` means none.
# A blank line or a line starting with `#` is ignored; any other row with a wrong shape refuses the table.
#   budget   <id>  <bytes>                   a file larger than <bytes> is reported, with the line that passes it
#   conflict <id>  <pattern a>  <pattern b>  <why they disagree>
#                                            a file with a line matching a and a line matching b is reported
#   name     <id>  <name>  <before>  <after> a skill name the text tells the worker to use: a lower-case
#                                            hyphenated word matching <name> anywhere, whose line text before it
#                                            matches <before> at its end and whose text after it matches <after>
#                                            at its start (the tool adds both anchors);
#                                            a name that is neither a skill (a SKILL.md in a skill folder
#                                            searched) nor a command (on PATH, or this repository's bin/ or
#                                            core/*/ and core/*/bin/ script of that name) is reported
#   ignore   <id>  <before>                  a name whose text before it matches <before> at its end is not checked
# The rows are pairs of words a person picked, never a model call, so a finding can be traced to its row.
# The tool only reports; a finding refuses nothing.
# The byte budget of a brief is not a row here: this table has no budget row, and bin/jg-brief-lint.sh
# takes the ceiling `ctx-worker-brief` from defaults/token-caps through bin/jg-context-load.sh. A table
# named with --rules may still carry one budget row of its own.
# A wait gets one status word. The shared brief says `paused:` and never `blocked:`, a home
# addition said every wait is `blocked:`, and a later one said a wait on your own work is `paused:`.
conflict
column5: one rule says a wait is `paused:` and not `blocked:`, the other says a wait is `blocked:`
